'''John H. Beynon''' [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]]<ref name="RS">{{cite web |url=https://royalsociety.org/people/john-beynon-11078/ |title=Professor John Beynon FRS |publisher=The Royal Society |accessdate=2016-03-22 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Boyd |first=Robert |date=2023 |title=John Herbert Beynon. 29 December 1923—24 August 2015 |journal=Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society |volume=73|pages=53–74 |doi=10.1098/rsbm.2023.0007 |doi-access=free }}</ref> (29 December 1923 – 24 August 2015) was a Welsh [[chemist]] and [[physicist]] known for his work in [[mass spectrometry]].<ref name="Cooks2016">{{cite journal|last1=Cooks|first1=Graham|title=John H. Beynon (1923–2015)|journal=Journal of the American Society for Mass Spectrometry|volume=27|issue=4|year=2016|pages=561–562|issn=1044-0305|doi=10.1007/s13361-016-1337-9|pmid=26832345|bibcode=2016JASMS..27..561C|s2cid=34383141}}</ref><ref name="Evans2013">{{cite web |url=http://www.cymruculture.co.uk/featuredarticles_87788.html |title=Scientists of Wales: Professor John H. Beynon, F.R.S. |last=Evans |first=Neville |work=Cymru Culture |date=1 September 2013 |accessdate=2016-03-27 }}</ref>

==Education and military service==
Beynon was born in the Welsh coal-mining town of Ystalyfera and was the older of two brothers. He went on to attend the University of Wales at Swansea (now Swansea University) in the early 1940s at the start of [[World War II]].<ref name="Maccoll1983">{{cite journal|last1=Maccoll|first1=Allan|title=J. H. Beynon|journal=Organic Mass Spectrometry|volume=18|issue=12|year=1983|pages=503–505|issn=0030-493X|doi=10.1002/oms.1210181202}}</ref>
<ref name="OH">{{cite web|author=Center for Oral History| title= John H. Beynon |url=https://oh.sciencehistory.org/oral-histories/beynon-john-h|website= [[Science History Institute]] }}</ref><ref name="CHF">{{cite book|first=Michael A. |last=Grayson |title=John H. Beynon, Transcript of an Interview Conducted by Michael A. Grayson at Swansea, Wales United Kingdom on 22 April 2008 |date= 22 April 2008 |url=https://oh.sciencehistory.org/sites/default/files/beynon_jh_0420_full.pdf|place=Philadelphia, PA|publisher=[[Science History Institute|Chemical Heritage Foundation]] }}</ref>
He received a B.S. in physics in 1943. He did not attend graduate school, instead deciding to join the [[Fighting Vehicles Research Establishment]] where he served between 1943 and 1947 developing tank [[fire-control system]]s.<ref name="NierYergey2015">{{cite book|author1=Keith A. Nier|author2=Alfred L. Yergey|author3=P. Jane Gale|title=The Encyclopedia of Mass Spectrometry: Volume 9: Historical Perspectives, Part B: Notable People in Mass Spectrometry|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=C02nBQAAQBAJ&pg=PA18|date=2 July 2015|publisher=Elsevier Science|isbn=978-0-08-100395-4|pages=18–}}</ref><ref name="Beynon1994">{{cite journal|last1=Beynon|first1=John H.|title=Letters to the editor|journal=Mass Spectrometry Reviews|volume=13|issue=2|year=1994|pages=183–185|issn=0277-7037|doi=10.1002/mas.1280130205|bibcode=1994MSRv...13..183B}}</ref>

==Career in industry==
Between the year 1947 and 1969, Beynon was Manager of Physics and Physical, Polymer and Analytical Chemistry at [[Imperial Chemical Industries]].<ref name="Williams1983">{{cite journal|last1=Williams|first1=A. E.|title=My years with John (1947–73)|journal=Organic Mass Spectrometry|volume=18|issue=12|year=1983|pages=506–508|issn=0030-493X|doi=10.1002/oms.1210181203}}</ref> 
Between 1947 and 1950, Beynon constructed what was to become the first mass spectrometer designed to study organic compounds unrelated to petroleum.<ref name="NierYergey2015" /><ref name="Beynon1991">{{cite journal|last1=Beynon|first1=J. H.|title=Mass spectrometry in retrospect: 25 years and more|journal=Organic Mass Spectrometry|volume=26|issue=5|year=1991|pages=353–358|issn=0030-493X|doi=10.1002/oms.1210260503}}</ref> He subsequently collaborated with [[Metropolitan-Vickers]] to produce the MS8 mass spectrometer, a prototype of the [[Associated Electrical Industries]] (AEI) MS9 mass spectrometer.<ref>{{cite journal|title=New Mass Spectrometer in Production|journal=Chemical & Engineering News|volume=40|issue=51|year=1962|pages=64–71|issn=0009-2347|doi=10.1021/cen-v040n051.p064}}</ref>

Beynon was made a senior research associate in 1964 which allowed him the opportunity to carry out his own research.<ref name="NierYergey2015" /> He was a Boomer Memorial Fellow at the [[University of Minnesota]] in 1965.

==Academic career==
Beynon took a position as Professor of Chemistry and Director of the Mass Spectrometry Center at [[Purdue University]] in 1968.<ref name="Cooks2004">{{cite journal|last1=Cooks|first1=R. Graham|title=John Beynon at Purdue|journal=Rapid Communications in Mass Spectrometry|volume=18|issue=1|year=2004|pages=7–10|issn=0951-4198|doi=10.1002/rcm.1303|pmid=14689550|bibcode=2004RCMS...18....7C}}</ref> In 1974 Beynon accepted a position as Royal Society Research Professor and Director of the Mass Spectrometry Research Unit at Swansea University.<ref name="Brenton2004">{{cite journal|last1=Brenton|first1=Gareth|title=John H. Beynon the Swansea years 1974–1986|journal=Rapid Communications in Mass Spectrometry|volume=18|issue=1|year=2004|pages=13–20|issn=0951-4198|doi=10.1002/rcm.1301|pmid=14689552|bibcode=2004RCMS...18...13B}}</ref>

==Awards and honours==
Beynon received the [[Sigma Xi]] Research Award, Purdue University in 1973, the Marice F. Hasler Award in 1979, the [[Jozef Stefan]] Medal in 1980, the Medal of the Serbian Chemical Society in 1981, the Techmart Trophy of the British Technology Group in 1984, the Jan Marc Marci Medal, Czechoslovak Spectroscopic Society in 1984, the [[International Mass Spectrometry Society]] Thomson Medal in 1985, the [[American Chemical Society]] Field and Franklin Award for Outstanding Work in Mass Spectrometry in 1987, the British Mass Spectrometry Society [[Aston Medal]] in 1998,<ref name="Games1990">{{cite journal|last1=Games|first1=D. E.|title=British Mass Spectrometry Society Aston Medal Awarded to Professor J. H. Beynon FRS|journal=Rapid Communications in Mass Spectrometry|volume=4|issue=11|year=1990|pages=491|issn=0951-4198|doi=10.1002/rcm.1290041109|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.bmss.org.uk/Docs%20histrory/Poster_beynon.pdf |title=Aston Medal 1990 John Herbert Beynon |last=Brenton |first=Gareth |work=BMSS Mass Matters |publisher=British Mass Spectrometry Society |year=2008 |accessdate=2016-03-22 |archive-date=17 February 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170217190325/http://www.bmss.org.uk/Docs%20histrory/Poster_beynon.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref> and the Italian Mass Spectrometry Society Gold Medal in 1990.<ref name="CHF" />

He was the Founder chairman British Mass Spectrometry Society (1960), a founding member of the American Society for Mass Spectrometry (1967), and Founder President of the European Mass Spectrometry Society (1993). Beynon was elected to the Royal Society in 1971.<ref name="RS" />

He authored over 350 scientific publications.<ref>{{cite journal|title=J. H. Beynon: List of publications|journal=Rapid Communications in Mass Spectrometry|volume=18|issue=1|year=2004|pages=24–36|issn=0951-4198|doi=10.1002/rcm.1307|pmid=14689556|bibcode=2004RCMS...18...24.|doi-access=free}}</ref> and several books on mass spectrometry.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Metastable Ions in Mass Spectrometry|journal=Analytical Chemistry|volume=46|issue=7|year=1974|pages=631A–632A|issn=0003-2700|doi=10.1021/ac60343a741}}</ref><ref name="Beynon1960">{{cite book|author=John Herbert Beynon|title=Mass spectrometry and its applications to organic chemistry|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=UlovAAAAIAAJ|year=1960|publisher=Elsevier Pub. Co.|isbn=9780444400475 }}</ref>

In 1987, Beynon was founding editor-in-chief of the journal ''[[Rapid Communications in Mass Spectrometry]]''.<ref name="Cooks2016" />
